title: Unresolved: Trump Pardon of Border Patrol Agents in Abuse Cases
description_short: Unresolved: Trump Pardon of Border Patrol Agents in Abuse Cases
description_medium: The supplied Associated Press URL was unavailable in earlier checks. DOJ’s 2025–present clemency table records dates, warrant links, districts, sentences and offenses; the returned entries include Jan. 2025 pardons of Ross Ulbricht and former D.C. officers Terence Sutton and Andrew Zabavsky. They do not resolve the alleged Border Patrol abuse cases. The packet still names no agents or case numbers and gives no source, baseline or period for the alleged rise in abuse reports. Timing alone cannot establish causation.
description_long: The packet attributes a 2025 pardon event to several Border Patrol agents convicted of abusing immigrants and alleges that abuse reports increased afterward. Its supplied Associated Press URL was unavailable in earlier checks. In this final focused check, the Justice Department’s Trump 2025–present clemency table and certificate-recipient release were accessible. The table’s returned entries identify dates, warrants, districts, sentences and offenses for other clemency grants, including January 2025 pardons of Ross Ulbricht and former D.C. officers Terence Sutton and Andrew Zabavsky; they did not resolve the alleged Border Patrol cases. The packet names no recipients, dockets, convictions or clemency warrants. It also provides no organization, dataset, baseline, period or count for the alleged increase in abuse reports. These gaps prevent distinguishing this claim from other law-enforcement pardons or assessing whether any change in complaints occurred. Even a documented rise after a pardon would not by itself show that the pardon caused it. Keep the entry on hold until case-specific clemency evidence and a dated complaint series are identified; do not substitute the separate 2020 Gary Brugman pardon.

supported_facts: The DOJ page heading is ‘Clemency Grants by President Donald J. Trump (2025-Present).’
The retrieved clemency table uses the columns ‘NAME and WARRANT,’ ‘DISTRICT,’ ‘SENTENCED,’ and ‘OFFENSE.’
The returned entries list Ross William Ulbricht under January 21, 2025, and Terence Dale Sutton, Jr. and Andrew Zabavsky under January 22, 2025, with their districts, sentences, and offenses.
exact_quotes: # Clemency Grants by President Donald J. Trump (2025-Present)

| Ross William Ulbricht | Southern District of New York | Life imprisonment; lifetime supervised release (May 29, 2015) | Aiding and abetting distribution of drugs over internet; continuing criminal enterprise; computer hacking conspiracy; fraud with identification documents; money laundering conspiracy |

| Terence Dale Sutton, Jr. | District of Columbia | 66 months' imprisonment; three years' supervised release, conditioned upon 100 hours' community service (September 12, 2024) | Murder in second degree; conspiracy; obstruction of justice and aiding and abetting |
| Andrew Zabavsky | District of Columbia | 48 months' imprisonment; three years' supervised release (September 12, 2024) | Conspiracy; obstruction of justice and aiding and abetting |
limitations: The returned entries do not identify the alleged Border Patrol recipients or cases. The partial retrieval cannot establish that no separate clemency action occurred.
